column14:
Step 1 - Visit official portal / nodal body: Open the scheme's official source (pib.gov.in) or contact the nodal body (Ministry of Finance/DFS). Read the latest guidelines, eligibility criteria, application window and forms here first, because scheme rules change often and third-party sites can be out of date.
Step 2 - Udyam Registration: Complete or verify your Udyam Registration at udyamregistration.gov.in. It is a free online registration that gives your business a Udyam number and certificate, which most MSME schemes use as proof that you are a registered micro, small or medium enterprise. Startups may need DPIIT/state startup recognition instead (see Remarks).
Step 3 - Register or log in on the application portal: Create an account or log in on the scheme's application portal using your mobile number, email and Aadhaar/PAN details. If the scheme is offline, approach the nodal office or bank branch directly and ask for the application form.
Step 4 - Fill in the application form: Fill in the form for 'Credit Guarantee Scheme for MSME Manufacturing' with business details (name, type, address, Udyam number), project details (what you will set up or expand and its cost) and financial details (turnover, existing loans, funding required). Keep numbers consistent with your project report and bank records.
Step 5 - Upload required documents: Upload or attach the documents: PAN, Udyam certificate, ID and address proof, project report (a written plan with costs and expected income), bank details and, if you claim a special benefit, a category certificate (SC/ST/OBC/women etc.). Scan clearly and check file size/format limits.
Step 6 - Submit for scrutiny: Submit the application. The nodal department or bank verifies your eligibility and documents. Expect queries, a site visit or requests for extra papers, and reply promptly to avoid rejection or delay.
Step 7 - Approval, disbursement and tracking: If approved, the benefit (subsidy, loan, guarantee or grant) is released or activated under the scheme's terms. Track the status on the portal or via the nodal office helpline, and keep the sanction letter and receipts for records.

column7: Delayed payment monitoring/redressal against buyers
column10: 1) Visit samadhaan.msme.gov.in 2) Register as a supplier MSME using Udyam number 3) File an online delayed-payment reference (Form) against the buyer 4) Case routed to the concerned Micro & Small Enterprise Facilitation Council (MSEFC) 5) Track hearing/resolution status on the portal.
column11: Yes - scheme-specific official process
column13: 1) Visit the Samadhaan portal | 2) Register as a supplier MSME | 3) File a delayed-payment reference | 4) Case goes to the MSEFC | 5) Track hearing and resolution
column14:
Step 1 - Visit the Samadhaan portal: Open samadhaan.msme.gov.in, the Ministry of MSME portal for recovering delayed payments from buyers.
Step 2 - Register as a supplier MSME: Register as a supplier using your Udyam number. Only registered micro and small enterprises that supplied goods or services can file.
Step 3 - File a delayed-payment reference: Fill in the online delayed-payment reference form against the buyer who has not paid: buyer details, invoice or order details, amount and due dates. Attach supporting invoices and correspondence.
Step 4 - Case goes to the MSEFC: The reference is routed to the Micro & Small Enterprise Facilitation Council (MSEFC) for your area, which takes it up through conciliation and, if needed, arbitration.
Step 5 - Track hearing and resolution: Follow hearing dates, notices and the final order on the portal until the dispute is resolved.

Step 1 - Do not apply to CGTMSE directly: CGTMSE does not take applications from businesses. The guarantee is a back-up cover for lenders.
Step 2 - Apply for a collateral-free loan at a lender: Apply for a collateral-free MSE loan at any Member Lending Institution (MLI), meaning a bank or NBFC that is enrolled with CGTMSE.
Step 3 - Bank assesses the proposal: The lender appraises your proposal under its own credit norms. The guarantee does not change the credit assessment.
Step 4 - Bank registers the loan and pays the fee: If the loan is sanctioned, the bank itself registers it with CGTMSE and pays the Annual Guarantee Fee.
Step 5 - Sign loan documents: You sign the normal loan documents. The guarantee cover is arranged bank-side through the CGTMSE portal (cgtmse.in).

Step 1 - Visit official portal / nodal body: Open the scheme's official source (startupgrantsindia.com) or contact the nodal body (Govt of Uttar Pradesh). Read the latest guidelines, eligibility criteria, application window and forms here first, because scheme rules change often and third-party sites can be out of date.
Step 2 - Udyam Registration: Complete or verify your Udyam Registration at udyamregistration.gov.in. It is a free online registration that gives your business a Udyam number and certificate, which most MSME schemes use as proof that you are a registered micro, small or medium enterprise. Startups may need DPIIT/state startup recognition instead (see Remarks).
Step 3 - Register or log in on the application portal: Create an account or log in on the scheme's application portal using your mobile number, email and Aadhaar/PAN details. If the scheme is offline, approach the nodal office or bank branch directly and ask for the application form.

Keep numbers consistent with your project report and bank records.
Step 5 - Upload required documents: Upload or attach the documents: PAN, Udyam certificate, ID and address proof, project report (a written plan with costs and expected income), bank details and, if you claim a special benefit, a category certificate (SC/ST/OBC/women etc.). Scan clearly and check file size/format limits.
Step 6 - Submit for scrutiny: Submit the application. The nodal department or bank verifies your eligibility and documents. Expect queries, a site visit or requests for extra papers, and reply promptly to avoid rejection or delay.
Step 7 - Approval, disbursement and tracking: If approved, the benefit (subsidy, loan, guarantee or grant) is released or activated under the scheme's terms. Track the status on the portal or via the nodal office helpline, and keep the sanction letter and receipts for records.
